observations.topic: lowercase weekday at the start of the composed divider label
observations.note: fr composes 'mardi à 14:30': {weekday} is formatDate(date,{weekday:'long'}) i.e. CLDR fr, lowercase by definition, and it lands at the start of a label where French capitalises. No catalogue spelling can fix it (the placeholder is inserted unchanged) and no text-transform:capitalize exists in the chat components (it would give 'Lundi À 14:30'). Formatter/component fix: capitalise the composed line's first character — harmless in en, whose weekdays already are. The same artifact reaches production via formatMessageDateTime's within-week branch, outside this key group. Not a defect of these four values.

{hour:'numeric'} is pinned for English byte-identity ('3:42 PM'), so fr prints '9:05' where the locale's own timeStyle:'short' is '09:05'. French time-of-day notation tolerates a one-digit hour ('9 h 05'), so this is a preference, not an error, and it is not a property of these keys (the sibling yesterday_at inherits it). Any fix is a locale-conditional 2-digit hour in src/i18n/format.ts.
